title.narrative: Women and Youth-Led transformative Climate Resilience (WY-LTCR)

description.narrative: The project aims to strengthen the resilience of marginalized communities in Porsha, Naogaon, with a particular focus on women and youth, through transformative climate adaptation, improved livelihoods, and enhanced access to public and private services. To ensure effective integration, the project will collaborate closely with Union Parishad, Upazila administration and line departments (such as Agriculture, Department of Agriculture Extension, Livestock, Youth Development, Women Affairs and Health) to align interventions with local development plans and leverage technical expertise. Partnerships with local NGOs, community-based organizations and the private sector will facilitate skill development, contribute to entrepreneurship promotion and market linkages. In a nutshell, the project will integrate efforts with local government, community institutions, NGOs and the private sector to strengthen community awareness and collaboration, enhance livelihood opportunities and improve access to safe drinking water and health services for inclusive and sustainable climate resilience actions. The above key strategies will function through building the technical capacity of local day laborers in mango garden management, facilitating linkages between women and youth with institutions, private sector actors, and local government for employment and enterprise support. Participatory water management committees will be established to ensure equitable access to safe water, while skill development and livelihood opportunities will enable local day laborers to increase income sustainability. The primary target groups are marginalized households, especially women and youth, who are facing vulnerabilities due to limited resources, restricted employment opportunities and climate related risks. The project will actively ensure gender-sensitive participation, addressing barriers such as women’s limited access to mango garden labor and youth’s lack of technical skills. Men and boys will also benefit through improved agricultural productivity and labor opportunities, while women and girls will gain enhanced access to income, vocational skills and community services. The ongoing Climate Change Program of CCDB focuses on transformative Locally-Led Adaptation (LLA), knowledge sharing, innovation, technology demonstration, capacity building, and strengthening community resilience to reduce risks for vulnerable populations. This project aligns with CCDB’s LLA approach. To build climate-resilient communities, the project will also develop synergies with CCDB-established community-based platforms in Ward No. 04. These CBOs were formed by local people from diverse occupations, as well as representatives from local governmental and non-governmental organizations, regardless of class, occupation, gender, caste, or religion.
